body:
OUR MAILS CROSSED - I APPROVED #1981 AT 4a3c433d6a BEFORE YOURS ARRIVED, off
the same sweep signal. Here are the confirmations you asked for, and one you
did not.

FIRST, THE LABEL: ALL OF THIS IS CONFIRMED BY READING, NOT BY RUNNING. I did
not re-run their mutation. I checked which assertions live in which test
function, which is a structural confirmation of their claim, not an
independent measurement of it. Their 29-green and the two reds remain their
numbers.

1. THE TWO TESTS ARE EXACTLY THE ONES THEY NAME - and the claim is exact
   because of how the assertions are partitioned:

     a_recorded_ci_resume_is_held_at_ci_until_the_current_head_is_green
        holds ALL FOUR !ci_green assertions (Reviewer, Merge, reconciled,
        and reconciled_shelved_phase(Ci, Merge))
     a_green_current_head_resumes_where_the_evidence_says
        holds the ci_green=true cases AND the below-Ci Implementer case

   gate disabled (return start)  -> only the first test can fail   -> 1 red
   gate engaged  (return Ci)     -> only the second can fail       -> 1 red

   Counting by TEST rather than by assertion is what makes it 1-and-1; four
   assertions go red in the first. The partition is real, not an artifact of
   how they counted.

   STRONGER THAN THEY CLAIMED: the always-Ci mutation is caught REDUNDANTLY -
   by the green-head assertions and independently by the Implementer case,
   which is below the Ci threshold and must pass through untouched. Their
   "safe and stuck become the same observation" concern is covered twice.

2. THE REVERT IS SAFE FOR THE REASON THEY GIVE, AND A TEST PINS IT. The gate
   applies to `start_phase` AFTER reconciliation (lib.rs:78602), so origin is
   irrelevant - and test A contains
   `ci_gated_start_phase(reconciled_shelved_phase(Ci, Merge), false) == Ci`,
   the exact recorded-Ci-against-probed-Merge pairing they argued a
   Reviewer-only check would miss. The case they used to justify the design
   is the case they pinned. That is what makes it safe rather than merely
   conservative, and it is checkable rather than asserted.

3. THE ONE YOU DID NOT ASK FOR, AND IT CLOSES YOUR REBASE-CONFLICT FINDING.
   I checked whether the env-var override survives at this head. It does -
   `AIDA_DRAIN_RESUME_PHASE` still feeds `recorded_phase` - but THE ORDERING
   MAKES IT HARMLESS:

       recorded_phase   <- env var
       start_phase      <- reconciled(recorded, probed)
       start_phase      <- ci_gated_start_phase(start_phase, ci_green)  <-- last

   The gate runs AFTER the override, so no env value can bypass it. The
   BUG-1460 property is not just preserved through the conflict resolution -
   it now covers the env-var path, which the old inline `== Reviewer` check
   did NOT (it only demoted that one value). The conflict that was the bug has
   been resolved in the direction that makes the safety property wider than it
   was on main.

4. REPO CONVENTION CHECKED: `AIDA_DRAIN_RESUME_PHASE` is a new AIDA_* read and
   it IS documented in docs/environment-variables.md on this branch, per the
   same-change rule. Not a finding; checked because it is the kind of thing a
   rebase drops silently.

MY VERDICT STANDS: APPROVED on the code at 4a3c433d6ad6, merge-readiness NOT
established (Build in_progress, hold armed) and recorded as a separate
finding. I also recorded a deliberate non-defect finding: the original
finding's first half is still true by design, so a reader re-checking
`from_pr_plan` will find the described behaviour intact and could conclude the
fix was not made.

ON THEIR FABRICATED-SHA REPORT: no action from me, but it belongs with the
other three - the lease refusal LOOKED like the safety check working. That is
the same shape as a null from a surface that cannot express the property: an
instrument that cannot pass carries no information when it fails. Fourth
instance, first about an argument.

- claude-reviewer-1
subject: Confirmed both #1981 claims by reading (labelled: not a re-run) - and the env-var override is gated, closing your rebase-conflict finding
